questions.question_text:
Two-stage screening surveys are commonly used to estimate the prevalence of psychiatric disorders in the community. In the �rst stage,
questionnaires are sent to a large sample of subjects. The results from this stage are scored and used to identify probable cases who are
then clinically interviewed. Which of the following is most likely to obscure true prevalence rates in such studies?
questions.explanation:
Selection bias occurs when study participants are selected in such a way that the association between exposure and disease di�ers for those
who participate and those who do not participate in the study. One type of selection bias seen especially in postal surveys is non-response
bias where responders who send their answers back to the researcher systematically di�er from non-responders. It is well established that
for lifestyle and behaviour related issues, non-responders often tend to have more problems than responders. This applies to mental health
issues as well.

options.text: The result is most likely to be an under-estimation of the satisfaction
Satisfaction is a normally distributed variable

correct_answer.text: Systematic di�erences exist between responders and non-responders

questions.explanation:
Satisfaction is not a normally distributed variable. It is likely that the 'most satis�ed' group responded while least satis�ed group abstained

Sending reminders can increase response rates. But randomly selecting responses that are returned will not provide any respite from non-

abstaining from returning the questionnaire. www.biomedcentral.com/1472-6963/4/31

Both smoking and alcohol consumption are associated with senile cognitive impairment. A study investigating the e�ect of smoking on
dementia fails to stratify exposed group according to drinking index. Which of the following can threaten the validity of conclusions derived
from this study?
questions.explanation:
A confounder is a factor that is associated both with the exposure of interest and the risk of the disease being studied. Thus, the observed
association between the exposure of interest and disease outcome may be incorrect. Confounding causes an error in comparisons between
groups if the groups are not strati�ed or adjusted.

questions.question_text:
Despite multiple reminders, a postal survey of heroin users to study disclosure to DVLA had a low response rate. What can be done to
improve the interpretation of conclusions from this survey?

options.text: Repharse the questionnaire and send the new version to nonresponders
Increase sample size by recruting another random group of users
Report the proportion of DVLA-disclosed responders as the lower limit of expected percentage of heroine users who have disclosed to
Ignore non responders and report on the available data
Compare and report the baseline characteristics of responders and non-responders

correct_answer.text: Compare and report the baseline characteristics of responders and non-responders

questions.explanation:
It is well established that survey nonresponders are probably di�erent from responders. It is likely that most nonresponders were
dissatis�ed with the service. Recruiting more people will not simply increase the response rate, and non-responders will probably exist in
equal numbers even in the second random group. The most one can do in this situation is to compare what is known about responders with
non-responders. This might throw some light on reasons for nonresponse and help deducting what direction their response might have
taken.

questions.explanation:

psychological factors such as motivation, productivity and most measures of self-report. The name derives from a factory called the
Hawthorne Works where experiments to improve worker productivity were carried out in the Industrial period. Surprisingly most of the

questions.question_text:
A scandalous tabloid report suggested that Asperger's syndrome may be more common in infants born to mothers who have irregular
periods in the year immediately preceding the birth. A medical charity funds a study to investigate this report. 100 mothers of children with
Asperger's syndrome were interviewed with respect to their menstrual history. 100 mothers of similar age and gender distributed normal
children were also interviewed. Which of the following may invalidate results in this study?
questions.explanation:
Recall bias is a type of information bias. It can be due to rumination bias - the presence of disease in�uences the perception of its causes or
exposure suspicion bias - the search for exposure to the putative cause once being diagnosed. Though it is classically associated with case-
control studies, it can also occur in cohort studies (for example, workers who known their exposure to hazardous substances may show a
trend to report more the e�ects related to them), and trials without participants' blinding. Delgado-Rodriguez and Llorca J. Bias. Journal Epid
Comm Health 2004;58;635-641

options.text: Lack of data on physical health

questions.explanation: It is highly likely that the untraced subjects in this study are actually deceased. In mortality studies, attrition bias is a very important concern.

questions.question_text:
The percentage of group members having quit smoking at post-test was found much higher in a group having received a quit-smoking
training program than in the control group in an RCT. Which of the following must be carefully checked while interpreting the study results?

options.text: Percentage completing the quit smoking program

correct_answer.text: Percentage completing the quit smoking program

questions.explanation:
Recall bias is unlikely in this scenario of a controlled trial; as the measurement pertains to percentage responders, regression towards the
mean is also unlikely. But presence of high drop out rates can bias the results as it is likely that those who will not be successful in quitting
will drop out of the program earlier than the ones who are more likely to succeed. This is important when considering translating evidence
to clinical practice.

questions.question_text:
It has been suggested that psychiatrists may investigate patients who use depot antipsychotics more often or more thoroughly for
metabolic disturbances than patients who do not. If this is true, then an apparent association between depot antipsychotics and
hypertriglyceridaemia can be due to
questions.explanation:
Surveillance bias, also called detection bias, occurs when one group is followed more closely than the other group.This could lead to an
outcome being diagnosed more often in the more closely followed group, but not because it truly occurred more often in that group.
